name: The Goats
hook: A mixed-race Philadelphia group who made a live-band political rap concept album about America's dark history, years before that was a known format.
blurb: Oatie Kato, Madd and Swayzack formed The Goats in Philadelphia in 1991, and they were the first act Ruffhouse Records signed. Their 1992 album Tricks of the Shade, co-produced by Oatie Kato and Ruffhouse co-founder Joe Nicolo, is a concept album: a story set during George H. W. Bush's presidency, using characters to walk through American history and politics, including what Columbus did to Native Americans. It shows that a openly political concept album was a working rap form by 1992. They played with a live band, with horns and piano, before The Roots made live-band rap famous in the same city, though no source consulted says The Roots took anything from them. Critics compared the album's range to De La Soul, Tribe and the Beastie Boys, and its politics to Public Enemy. It got strong reviews but didn't sell well. The group made one more album and broke up.
